\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সতর্ক} (sôtôrkô)}{সতর্ক (sôtôrkô)}]{\bn{সতর্ক} (sôtôrkô) — alert; on guard}

\label{lesson:BN-C294-sotorko}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for destruction, then the Bengali for to be trapped underneath.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সতর্ক}}
\textbf{\bn{সতর্ক}} — \emph{sôtôrkô} — \textquotedblleft{}alert; on guard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রেডিওতে} \bn{সবাইকে} \bn{সতর্ক} \bn{থাকতে} \bn{বলল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{reḍiote sôbāike sôtôrkô thākte bôllô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The radio told everyone to stay alert.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সতর্ক}} (\emph{sôtôrkô}) is Sanskrit \emph{satarka}, 'with reasoning', and so 'cautious' (Monier-Williams): \emph{sa-}, 'with', and \emph{tarka}, 'reasoning' — \textbf{\bn{তর্ক}}, in Bengali, is an argument.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôtôrkô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôtôrkô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reḍiote sôbāike sôtôrkô thākte bôllô.} — The radio told everyone to stay alert.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for destruction, then the Bengali for to be trapped underneath, then say \emph{sôtôrkô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সতর্ক} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Alert; on guard\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সাবধান} (sābdhān)}{সাবধান (sābdhān)}]{\bn{সাবধান} (sābdhān) — careful; watch out}

\label{lesson:BN-C294-sabdhan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to be trapped underneath, then the Bengali for alert.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সাবধান}}
\textbf{\bn{সাবধান}} — \emph{sābdhān} — \textquotedblleft{}careful; watch out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সাবধান}, \bn{সিঁড়িটা} \bn{ভাঙা}!
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sābdhān, sĩṛiṭā bhāngā!}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Careful, the stairs are broken!
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সাবধান}} (\emph{sābdhān}) is Sanskrit \emph{sāvadhāna}, 'attentive, careful' (Monier-Williams): \emph{sa-}, 'with', and \emph{avadhāna}, 'attention'. Said alone it is a warning: \bn{সাবধান}!
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sābdhān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sābdhān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sābdhān, sĩṛiṭā bhāngā!} — Careful, the stairs are broken!
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to be trapped underneath, then the Bengali for alert, then say \emph{sābdhān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সাবধান} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Careful; watch out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সংকেত} (sôngket)}{সংকেত (sôngket)}]{\bn{সংকেত} (sôngket) — a signal; a warning sign}

\label{lesson:BN-C294-songket}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for alert, then the Bengali for careful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সংকেত}}
\textbf{\bn{সংকেত}} — \emph{sôngket} — \textquotedblleft{}a signal; a warning sign\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বন্দরে} \bn{বিপদের} \bn{সংকেত} \bn{দেখে} \bn{জেলেরা} \bn{সমুদ্রে} \bn{গেল} \bn{না।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bôndôre bipôder sôngket dekhe jelerā sômudre gelô nā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When they saw the danger signal at the port, the fishermen didn't go to sea.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সংকেত}} (\emph{sôngket}) is Sanskrit \emph{saṃketa}, 'an agreement, a convention' (Monier-Williams); a storm signal is a sign everyone has agreed to read the same way.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôngket}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôngket}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bôndôre bipôder sôngket dekhe jelerā sômudre gelô nā.} — When they saw the danger signal at the port, the fishermen didn't go to sea.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for alert, then the Bengali for careful, then say \emph{sôngket} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সংকেত} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A signal; a warning sign\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আশঙ্কা} (āshôngkā)}{আশঙ্কা (āshôngkā)}]{\bn{আশঙ্কা} (āshôngkā) — a fear; an apprehension}

\label{lesson:BN-C294-ashongka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for careful, then the Bengali for a warning sign.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আশঙ্কা}}
\textbf{\bn{আশঙ্কা}} — \emph{āshôngkā} — \textquotedblleft{}a fear; an apprehension\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আবহাওয়া} \bn{খারাপ}, \bn{তাই} \bn{বন্যার} \bn{আশঙ্কা} \bn{আছে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ābôhāoyā khārāp, tāi bônyār āshôngkā āchhe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather is bad, so a flood is feared.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আশঙ্কা}} (\emph{āshôngkā}) is Sanskrit \emph{āśaṅkā}, 'fear, apprehension; doubt' (Monier-Williams). It is the fear that something will happen, not fear of a thing in front of you.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āshôngkā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āshôngkā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ābôhāoyā khārāp, tāi bônyār āshôngkā āchhe.} — The weather is bad, so a flood is feared.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for careful, then the Bengali for a warning sign, then say \emph{āshôngkā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{আশঙ্কা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fear; an apprehension\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{এড়ানো} (eṛāno)}{এড়ানো (eṛāno)}]{\bn{এড়ানো} (eṛāno) — to avoid}

\label{lesson:BN-C294-erano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a warning sign, then the Bengali for an apprehension.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{এড়ানো}}
\textbf{\bn{এড়ানো}} — \emph{eṛāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to avoid\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমরা} \bn{বড়} \bn{রাস্তা} \bn{এড়িয়ে} \bn{গলি} \bn{দিয়ে} \bn{গেলাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmrā bôṛo rāstā eṛiye gôli diye gelām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We avoided the main road and went through the lanes.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{বিপদ} \bn{এড়ালেন}, \emph{tini bipôd eṛālen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{এড়ানো}} (\emph{eṛāno}) is filed in CDIAL 2511 under Sanskrit \emph{\'{\={e}}ṭatē}, 'goes', which lists Bengali \emph{eṛāna}, 'to avoid', beside \emph{eṛā}, 'to let go, reject'; how the sense moved is not set out there. The -\bn{এ} form is \bn{এড়িয়ে}: \bn{এড়িয়ে} \bn{গেলাম}, I steered clear.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṛāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṛāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmrā bôṛo rāstā eṛiye gôli diye gelām.} — We avoided the main road and went through the lanes.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a warning sign, then the Bengali for an apprehension, then say \emph{eṛāno} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{এড়ানো} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To avoid\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
